description: VoxCPM2: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Multilingual Speech Generation, Creative Voice Design, and True-to-Life Cloning

summary.one_liner: VoxCPM2 is an open-source, tokenizer-free text-to-speech model (2B parameters, Python/PyTorch) that supports 30 languages, voice design from text descriptions, voice cloning, and 48kHz output.
summary.what_it_does: VoxCPM generates continuous speech representations with an end-to-end diffusion autoregressive architecture rather than discrete audio tokens. VoxCPM2, the current release, is a 2B-parameter model built on a MiniCPM-4 backbone and trained on over 2 million hours of multilingual speech, per the README. It synthesizes text in 30 listed languages plus several Chinese dialects without a language tag. Voice Design creates a voice from a natural-language description with no reference audio. Controllable Cloning clones a voice from a short reference clip with optional style guidance, and Ultimate Cloning continues from a reference audio plus its transcript. The README also describes 16kHz reference input with 48kHz output via AudioVAE V2. The repo covers Python API, CLI, web demo, fine-tuning (SFT and LoRA) scripts, and benchmark tables, and it links to vLLM-Omni, llama.cpp-omni, and Nano-vLLM serving options.
use_cases: clone a voice from a short audio clip
design a new synthetic voice from a text description
serve TTS through an OpenAI-compatible API
fine-tune a TTS model on a specific speaker
run text-to-speech on-device with GGUF weights
notable: Tokenizer-free diffusion autoregressive TTS producing continuous speech latents
Voice Design from natural-language descriptions with no reference audio
Ultimate cloning that continues from reference audio plus transcript
48kHz output from 16kHz reference audio via AudioVAE V2
Multiple serving paths: Python API, vLLM-Omni, llama.cpp-omni GGUF builds
caveats: Voice Design and controllable cloning results can vary between runs; the README suggests trying 1 to 3 times
Language coverage is limited to the 30 listed languages; others are untested unless fine-tuned
README reports ~8 GB VRAM for VoxCPM2 and RTF ~0.30 on RTX 4090 with standard PyTorch; faster paths need extra engines
Voice cloning carries misuse risk; the README forbids impersonation, fraud, or disinformation
